refuted_claims: CFO Q1'26: 'a recovery in loan origination volume to RMB38.5 billion' - the company's own tables show mainland volume RMB38.7bn (Q4'25) -> RMB38.5bn (Q1'26) = -0.5% SEQUENTIALLY. No recovery. REFUTED.

CFO Q1'26: 'Early signs of credit recovery' - 90d+ delinquency went 2.85% -> 3.11% over the same quarter, and the release's own vintage JPEG puts 2025Q2/2025Q3 at/above every prior cohort at equal seasoning. REFUTED.

'Two-engine model' / overseas as the growth engine - Q1'26 segment table: Overseas = 29.6% of revenue but 7.6% of segment profit at a 4.8% operating margin on a ~110%-APR product; mainland segment profit fell RMB314.4M while overseas rose RMB21.4M, replacing 6.8% of the loss. REFUTED AS FRAMED.
honesty_finding.confirmed_but_misattributed: '+6.2% sequential revenue' (RMB3,023.9M -> 3,210.1M) is arithmetically true, but the driver was net interest income +100.6% YoY (moving loans onto the balance sheet; provision for loans receivable +155.4%), NOT volume. The revenue gain was bought with balance-sheet credit risk and then attributed to a volume recovery the company's own table shows did not occur.
honesty_finding.mechanism: masking channel = causal misattribution of a sequential revenue gain, wrapped in a sequential-vs-YoY frame switch (-7.8% YoY revenue and -44.4% YoY profit are never spoken aloud; '+6.2% sequentially' is). signal channel = the company's own volume table and the vintage-curve JPEG in the SAME 6-K. signal-to-price latency ~ZERO - everything needed to refute it shipped in the same filing, and the tape still paid +16.9% that week.

regulatory_sequence_live: 2025-04-03 issued / 2025-10-01 effective: NFRA Notice on Strengthening the Supervision of Online Lending Business - bank whitelists; platforms barred from charging borrowers; credit-enhancers barred from service/consultation fees (disguised fee-stacking); comprehensive cost inside the SPC 24% ceiling; extends to consumer-finance and trust companies (closes the funding-partner workaround)

2026-08-01 EFFECTIVE (two days ago): NFRA+PBoC Provisions on Disclosure of the Comprehensive Borrowing Costs for Personal Loan Business - itemized disclosure of every fee and its collecting entity; the enforcement mechanism for the 24% all-in ceiling

2026-09-30 EFFECTIVE: PBoC/NFRA/CAC +5 agencies Administrative Measures for Online Marketing of Financial Products - bans routing to unlicensed third parties, bans 'low threshold'/'drawdown in seconds'/'low interest rate' ad language, bans algorithmic inducement. Attacks customer acquisition directly; the 20-F itself says it 'would affect user acquisition'

2026-04-01 EFFECTIVE: Philippines SEC memorandum - 12%/month effective-rate cap on consumer loans <=P10,000 with terms <=4 months. Not yet in any reported quarter; hits the 4.8%-margin overseas segment from Q2'26

CONSTRUCTIVE: Indonesia OJK abandoned the uniform 0.1%/day-by-2026 plan (2024-12-31, reiterated by regulation 2025-07-31) for tenor-differentiated 0.3% (<=6mo) / 0.2% (>6mo); FinVolution's Indonesian tenor is 3-4 months, so the cap is non-binding. The largest overseas bear leg is RETIRED.
guide_arithmetic: Q1'26 revenue RMB3.21bn x4 = RMB12.84bn, already the TOP of the RMB11.5-12.9bn FY26 guide. For the midpoint to hold, Q2-Q4 must average RMB3.00bn - i.e. revenue must FALL from here. Either the guide is sandbagged or the Aug-1 and Sep-30 rules are expected to bite. The Q2 print resolves which. Note Q1 has historically been the STRONGEST quarter (FY25: Q1 746 / Q2 ~697 / Q3 641 / Q4 416 RMB m), so annualizing Q1 is generous, not conservative.

edge_explainer.market_believes: A cheap, cash-rich, 19%-shareholder-yield Chinese fintech at 5x forward and 0.5x book, with an accelerating overseas growth engine, whose regulatory shock is now behind it.
edge_explainer.we_believe: The regulatory shock is not behind it - two further rules took effect 2026-08-01 and take effect 2026-09-30, and the Philippines cap hit on 2026-04-01 and has never appeared in a reported quarter. The 'overseas growth engine' is 29.6% of revenue at a 4.8% operating margin and replaced 6.8% of what the domestic profit engine lost. Credit is deteriorating on the company's own unseasoned vintages. Management's Q1 story - volume recovering, credit recovering - is refuted by tables in the same filing; the sequential revenue gain came from taking balance-sheet credit risk, not from volume. This is a statutory reconstruction priced as a sentiment de-rate.
edge_explainer.why_we_might_have_edge: Three sources, all primary: (1) the vintage-loss chart is published ONLY as a JPEG and is invisible to text extraction - reading it multimodally shows the two freshest cohorts are the worst in four years; (2) the segment table published for the first time this quarter quantifies that the marketed growth engine earns a 4.8% margin; (3) the 20-F filed 2026-04-29 dates two further rules into August and September 2026 that every 'China risk has settled' note treats as historical.
edge_explainer.why_it_might_be_priced_in: Strongly possible, and honestly the binding uncertainty. At 4.8x forward on falling earnings with $870M of net financial cash assigned ~zero value, the market is already pricing a value trap. The stock rallied +16.9% on the last print and has chopped flat for ten weeks - it may simply be waiting, correctly, at a correct price. Without consensus data I cannot close this. That is why the ruling is REJECT-and-watch, not SHORT.
edge_explainer.what_resolves_it: The Q2'26 print (~2026-08-19/20): mainland volume vs the RMB50.8bn base, the 90d+ delinquency print, whether the FY26 guide survives its first contact with the August-1 disclosure rules, and the Q2 vintage chart.
edge_explainer.mechanism_falsifier: Mainland volume comping better than -15% YoY WITH delinquency turning down would say the level shift is ending faster than modelled - the freezable grades exactly this, and a miss sends the name straight back to court as a re-rate candidate.
edge_explainer.edge_type: negative edge - the reject IS the position; a re-open ladder rests below, with the capital-return expression the only survivor
